name: Ives II
award: 2025 Federal 9% (Round One) and 4% housing tax credits (paired)
headline: Foothills Regional Housing (the Jefferson County Housing Authority) is developing Ives II, a 98-unit, four-story family rental at 7525 W. 44th Ave. in Wheat Ridge for households at 30% to 70% AMI, financed by a 54-unit 9% award and a 44-unit 4% bond award that CHFA made in 2025.
why_it_matters: It is a working example of pairing a 9% award with a 4% bond deal in one building: the housing authority used its own bond cap and city-donated land to reach 98 units where a 9% award alone would have funded 54.

status.label: Groundbreaking scheduled 2026-07-24; financing closing and building permit not confirmed
status.detail: Jefferson County's calendar listed an Ives II groundbreaking for 2026-07-24. Hoodline reported on 2026-07-25 that the county commissioners approved a property tax exemption and bonds, that demolition was complete, and that the remaining financing and final permits were still needed before vertical construction. No public record of the financing closing or a building permit was found.

next_step: Watch for a City of Wheat Ridge building permit for 7525 W. 44th Ave. and a recorded CHFA land use restriction agreement, which would confirm the financing closed.

key_numbers.value: 98 homes: 54 under the 9% award, 44 under the 4% award
key_numbers.meaning: One building, split into two tax credit pieces. All units serve 30% to 70% AMI; one unit in the 4% piece is not income-restricted.

key_numbers.value: $1,600,000 a year in federal 9% credit plus $772,287 a year in federal 4% credit

Issued by the Jefferson County Housing Authority (the sponsor itself) for the 4% piece, per CHFA's 4% award report.

background.text: How the pieces fit: one 98-unit building is split into two tax credit projects. The competitive 9% award funds 54 units and a noncompetitive 4% award, backed by tax-exempt bonds, funds the other 44. Each piece also got $650,000 of state credit and a TOC credit.

The applicant says this is a change from its 2024 application: it added a 4% piece using Foothills Regional Housing's own bond cap to reach 98 units, which it says is more cost-efficient and was preferred by neighbors.

CHFA's 2025 state credit annual report lists Ives II twice: 54 units under state and federal 9% credit and 44 units under federal 4% and noncompetitive state credit, both with TOC credit. Foothills Regional Housing's development chief is quoted saying 20% of the equity for the 98 units comes from the state credit.

In July 2024, before the CHFA application, Foothills Regional Housing told Wheat Ridge council that Ives phase 2 needed about $20 million to complete, and that it had no approved site plan or building permit yet.

The applicant says the site is correctly zoned and could close within nine months of an award. A single-story bank building had to be demolished, adding about $250,000. Stormwater detention goes on the roof because the infill site is tight.

The Phase I environmental report found one recognized environmental condition. The plan includes a groundwater-use restriction, a soils management plan, sub-slab vapor mitigation and radon mitigation.

The project grew between rounds: CHFA's December 2024 letter-of-intent report lists the 9% piece at 50 units with a $65,000 TOC request; the February 2025 applicant report and the award list 54 units and $70,200.
Services: residents can use Jefferson Center for Mental Health services at Ives I next door, and Developmental Disability Resource Center will provide other services.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's 4% award report gives $11.2 million in private activity bonds for the 4% piece, while Hoodline reports the county authorized $6.6 million in bonds in July 2026.

The 9% narrative describes 54 one-bedroom, 36 two-bedroom and 8 three-bedroom units (98), while CHFA's award descriptions list 53 one-bedroom, 36 two-bedroom and 8 three-bedroom units (97), because the 4% piece's mix covers only 43 of its 44 units.
